rows.rule: A charge fails only if no arrangement can reach ER of every target, avoid non-target ER and keep coherency. The engine's heuristic matches the row; it may fail a possible charge in odd geometry. This is an accepted shortcut.
rows.source: core: Charging with a Unit; src/engine/phases/charge.ts:10-20
rows.fix: None required. Optional: before failing, accept a player-submitted arrangement validated by chargeMoveRejection; log heuristic charge failures in sim to measure how often they happen.

rows.rule: Core (Charging with a Unit): a charging model must end in base contact with an enemy model only if it can while the unit still meets every charge condition (ER of every target, no ER of non-targets, coherency, no moving through enemy models). Model order is the controller's choice.
rows.source: core: Charging with a Unit; src/engine/phases/charge.ts:422 couldReachBaseContact, :366 chargeMoveRejection
rows.fix: couldReachBaseContact tests a straight-line contact spot for budget, board, blockers, non-target ER and end terrain only. It never checks coherency of the arrangement with the model moved there, pathCrossesModels against targets/non-targets, or crossesImpassable. Add those checks. Effect: legal player moves are rejected, and legalChargeMoves can declare a reachable charge failed.

rows.rule: Core, Movement phase > Move Units: the pass-through rule is worded for every time a model moves (not just Normal/Advance/Fall Back). Models may pass through friendly models; a MONSTER or VEHICLE may not pass through a friendly MONSTER or VEHICLE. Charge, Pile In and Consolidate grant no exemption. FLY handled separately.
rows.source: core: Move Units; src/engine/phases/movement.ts:285-304 (bigFriendly) vs charge.ts:342 and fight.ts:230/535
rows.fix: Charge (checkChargeArrangement plus planner/repair) and fight pile-in/consolidate never check movers that are MONSTER/VEHICLE against friendly MONSTER/VEHICLE models (geometry.checkPlacements only tests end overlap). Add the movement.ts bigFriendly path test to charge.ts and fight.ts, skipped for FLY.

rows.rule: Fire Overwatch is used in the opponent's Movement/Charge phase. A Heroic Intervention charge happens in the charger-owner's own turn, so they cannot Overwatch it. The out-of-phase rule also bars other phase rules during HI.
rows.source: core: Fire Overwatch, Heroic Intervention, Out-of-Phase Rules
rows.fix: None.

rows.rule: Rules Commentary (Pile-in Move): each moving model must end closer to the closest enemy model, and in base contact with that closest model if possible. The unit must end in coherency and within ER. Consolidate works the same way. The heuristic planner is an acceptable shortcut.
rows.source: core: Pile In, Consolidate; rulesCommentary: Pile-in Move; src/engine/phases/fight.ts:258 couldReachBaseContact, :711
rows.fix: fight.ts couldReachBaseContact loops over every enemy, so it forces contact with any enemy model. Test only the model's closest enemy model at the start of its move (the same model closerToClosestEnemyAtStart uses), and require the arrangement to stay coherent with the model there. Otherwise legal pile-ins are rejected and the AI may fall back to not moving.

rows.rule: 'Closest' means closest to the model using the rule; when tied, its controller picks. Measuring at the start of that model's move is the standard reading.
rows.fix: Optional: on ties (within EPS), accept 'closer to any tied-closest enemy' instead of whichever is found first.

rows.rule: Random characteristics are rolled per model/weapon when needed. Melee targets and splits are declared before any attack resolves. The rules don't say whether A is rolled before the split; rolling first is common table practice and has no downside.
rows.source: core: Random Characteristics, Fight Select Targets
rows.fix: None. Keep Command Re-roll available on the attack-number roll (attacksFor rollExpr purpose 'attacks').

rows.rule: A model fights with one melee weapon and, for multi-profile weapons, one declared profile. Data stores profiles as separate ids (profileGroup), e.g. GK Nemesis greatsword strike/sweep, and resolveModelWeapons offers them as a choice.
rows.source: core: Select Weapon; fight.ts:306; grey-knights weapons.json
rows.fix: Doc only: the 'neither occurs in CP data' claim in fight.ts:20-23 and the row is out of date. The Dreadknight's two profiles are handled by the existing meleeWeapon choice.

rows.rule: Counter-offensive: just after an enemy unit fought, your unit (not yet selected to fight) fights next. Core alternation has players take turns selecting units, and the CO unit is a selection, so the opponent selects after it. No official FAQ settles this. The engine comment marks its reading as [interp].
rows.fix: Trace: A's unit finishes, nextToSelect=B, B uses CO, mark saves B, CO unit finishes, B selects again. When B had eligible units, B gets two activations in a row. In finishUnit, for a CO resume set nextToSelect=otherPlayer(CO unit's player). Keep the restore for Death Blow (a faction insertion). Update FIGHT-025 and spec R-9.12.

rows.rule: Tank Shock is only usable in your own Charge phase, after your VEHICLE ends a Charge move. Heroic Intervention happens in the opponent's Charge phase, resolved as if it were yours. The out-of-phase rule (core and Rules Commentary) forbids other rules for that phase, so no Tank Shock after a Heroic Intervention.
rows.source: core: Tank Shock, Heroic Intervention, Out-of-Phase Rules; src/engine/stratagems.ts:150-152; code-hooks.ts:450; charge.ts:5-7
rows.fix: In stratagems.ts timingOk, remove the tankShockMortalWounds exception for a non-active player. Fix the comments in code-hooks.ts:450 and charge.ts:5-7, and invert the STRAT-018 interp test so Tank Shock is not offered after HI.

rows.rule: Tank Shock picks an enemy unit in ER and a VEHICLE model of the charging unit in ER of it. Roll D6 equal to that model's T; each 5+ is 1 MW, max 6.
rows.fix: None (apart from RC-041). The hook checks the same unit, model ownership and model-in-ER; it rolls T dice at 5+ with a cap of 6.

rows.rule: Epic Challenge: when your CHARACTER unit within ER of an Attached unit is selected to fight, one CHARACTER model gains Precision on melee attacks until end of phase.
rows.fix: None. The hook checks: selected unit is yours, enemy isAttached (cleared when a half dies), model in the selected unit, units engaged; Precision goes to that model only.

rows.rule: Counter-offensive: just after an enemy unit has fought (consolidation included), target your unit within ER of enemies that hasn't been selected to fight.
rows.fix: None. The window fires after consolidate, the hook requires an enemy trigger and inEngagementWithEnemy, and the data requires notYetFought. For sequencing see RC-040.

rows.rule: A unit with models carrying different keywords has all of them and is affected by rules for any of them. 'Non-KEYWORD' rules apply only to units without it. Attached units are one unit for all rules.
rows.fix: None. The any-half match and any-half exclusion are correct.

rows.rule: Simultaneous rules during a turn are ordered by the active player. The engine uses a fixed order: on defensive windows the defender goes first, which gives the active player the information edge they would choose. Elsewhere collisions are rare.
rows.fix: None. Optional: let the active player choose the order if a real two-sided collision turns up.

rows.rule: No CP datasheet has GRENADES, so Grenade is never legal. Armoured Sentinels have SMOKE (Smokescreen legal), and VEHICLE units exist in several patrols (Tank Shock legal). The engine filters stratagem targets by keyword, and no code reads params.combatPatrol.legal. Play is correct; only the docs are stale.
rows.source: cpFactions keyword lines; src/data/core/stratagems.json:99,127,217; src/data/factions/astra-militarum/datasheets/armoured-sentinels.json:12; docs/spec/11-combat-patrol.md CP-1.6
rows.fix: No engine change. Docs only: rewrite 11-combat-patrol.md CP-1.6, and update the smokescreen (legal:false) and tank-shock ('Ork VEHICLE only') notes in stratagems.json. astra-militarum.md already states this. AST-001 claims a Sentinel Smokescreen check; confirm the test asserts it.

rows.rule: CP: a secured marker stays yours with no models in range. It stops being secured if the opponent controls it at the end of a later Command phase. Rules Commentary (Objective Secured), for any such ability: control is still checked at each phase and turn end, and a higher enemy LoC takes control then.
rows.source: combatPatrol: Securing Objective Markers; rulesCommentary: Objective Secured; src/engine/objectives.ts:118-140; src/engine/missions.ts:72-74; spec CP-2.5 [interp]
rows.fix: evaluateControl and liveController make the securer win every evaluation regardless of LoC (the CP-2.5 literal interp). Instead: opponent LoC > securer's means the opponent controls at that check; clear securedBy only at a Command-phase end; with no higher enemy LoC, control falls back to the securer. Also check the securedBy shortcuts in factions/adepta-sororitas.ts:153 and grey-knights.ts:173. Affects end-of-turn and round-5 scoring.

rows.rule: CP: if a player has no models at the start of their turn, the other may play out their turns until round 5. Unarrived Reserves are still army models until the round-3 cull. Both tabled isn't covered; ending at once changes nothing.
rows.fix: None. Make sure end-of-battle scoring (e.g. secondaries) still runs on an early end.

rows.rule: Bag the Big 'Un (Morgrim's Butchas): pick an enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE model (else the enemy WARLORD). At battle end, 8VP if it was destroyed by any means, 12VP if your Beastboss destroyed it. CP: Reserves not arrived by end of round 3 count as destroyed.
rows.source: cpFactions morgrim-s-butchas; combatPatrol Reserves; src/engine/missions.ts:266-286; src/engine/phases/movement.ts:500-517
rows.fix: The cull sets location 'destroyed' without destroyedBy (only attack.ts destroyUnitTail sets it), so the target scores 0 and the 'reserves' branch never runs. Return unitPoints when location==='destroyed' && !destroyedBy. Also: the rule targets a model, but the engine needs the whole unit destroyed. Latent until the roster is in data.

rows.rule: CP: +10VP at battle end for a fully painted Battle Ready army. A symmetric constant never changes the result.
rows.fix: None. Optional: default both players to 10 so VP totals match tabletop scores.

rows.rule: Objective markers (40mm) should be more than 1" from impassable terrain parts (e.g. ruin walls). The 1.414" clearance is measured from the marker centre; in cp-05, markers b and c are 0.63" (edge) from solid crates. Ruins are fine.
rows.source: core: Objective Markers and Terrain Features; src/data/terrain/cp-01.json
rows.fix: Owner call: do climbable 3" crates count as impassable? If yes, move container-1/2 at least 0.4" further from b/c in cp-01.json. Either way, update the 11-combat-patrol.md §3 footprint table.

rows.rule: Level of Control is the sum of in-range models' OC including modifiers. Battle-shocked units add 0, and so do Death Blow models awaiting removal. This is a HUD-only deviation; engine scoring uses objectives.ts levelOfControl, which applies hookService.statFor and pendingRemoval.
rows.source: core: Objective Markers; src/client/board/controlLevels.ts:13-28; src/engine/objectives.ts:95-107; src/engine/index.ts DEFAULT_SERVICES
rows.fix: DEFAULT_SERVICES is exported as a value from @/engine (the file header claiming otherwise is stale), so liveControlLevels can return DEFAULT_SERVICES.objectives.levelOfControl(state, objectiveId). Delete the client recompute and its comment.

rows.rule: Presentation only: the engine's stratagem legality check is final, so play is unaffected.
rows.fix: Optional: DEFAULT_SERVICES.stratagems is an exported value, so the panel could use the engine's real target/condition check instead of the CP/limit approximation.

rows.rule: Presentation only: the engine validates the pivot-aware path. Straight-line preview is more permissive, so a previewed move may be rejected but never wrongly allowed.
rows.fix: None.

rows.rule: Presentation only: the engine still rolls and applies battle-shock and Desperate Escape. director.ts has no BattleShockTested/DesperateEscapeRolled cases.
rows.fix: Optional: map BattleShockTested and DesperateEscapeRolled events to dice-tray requests in director.ts.

rows.rule: No rules effect: the watchdog force-answers with a RandomDecider choosing from engine legalActions, so forced moves are always legal. Ignoring stratagems is an AI-strength issue.
rows.fix: None for rules.

rows.rule: No rules effect: the expected-damage heuristics only steer bot choices; the engine resolves attacks exactly. The header at src/ai/expected.ts:4 matches the row.
